archived_because: Revised development case: the report now restates that the affected routings carry 38% of purchase volume (so 15.2% remains delayed) and evidences the December 9 knowledge date and the January 8 forecast refresh required by version 1.1.

event.title: Rerouting and freight surcharge update

sources.text: Synthetic scenario document for the Crocs hypothetical private-credit scenario. Operations update dated January 15, 2027. 60% of the affected volume has been rebooked through United States West Coast ports with rail to the distribution center, which cuts the delay on that portion from 24 days to 9 days. The remaining 40% of the affected volume still moves around the Cape with a 24-day delay. No further alternative capacity is available before April 2027.

Synthetic scenario document for the Crocs hypothetical private-credit scenario. Incremental freight cost for the first quarter of 2027 is estimated at $6.8 million. Wholesale customers representing most of the affected volume accepted a freight surcharge from February 1, 2027 that recovers 45% of the incremental cost, leaving about $3.7 million unrecovered. The surcharge does not apply to direct-to-consumer sales.

Synthetic scenario document for the Crocs hypothetical private-credit scenario. The 13-week cash forecast required after the disruption was delivered on December 22, 2026. Its low point was $48.9 million in February 2027.

analysis.summary: The Jan 15 2027 rerouting shows 40 % of the affected volume still faces a 24‑day delay, which could push lead times above 70 days for ≥10 % of volume, weakening the lead‑time stability assumption. Freight cost data reveal only 45 % recovery of a $6.8 M incremental cost, short of the assumed ~50 % recovery, challenging the freight‑recovery assumption. The 13‑week cash forecast was delivered before the disruption, missing the C06 deadline, while notice and cash‑report duties lack sufficient evidence to judge compliance.

attributions.rationale: Event shows 40 % of the affected volume experiences a 24‑day delay; if that volume is ≥10 % of total purchase volume, lead time would exceed 70 days for that portion, meeting the review criterion for lead‑time instability.

evidence.quote: The remaining 40% of the affected volume still moves around the Cape with a 24-day delay.

missing_information: Proportion of the affected volume relative to the borrower’s total purchase volume

covenant_assessments.rationale: Knowledge of a supply disruption on 2027-01-15 triggered a duty to deliver a 13‑week cash forecast within 10 Business Days (by 2027-02-09). The forecast was delivered on 2026-12-22, before the knowledge date, so the duty was missed.

evidence.quote: The 13-week cash forecast required after the disruption was delivered on December 22, 2026. Its low point was $48.9 million in February 2027.
